rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon split as one of its signs of approach.
rows.anchor: { اقتربت الساعة } دنت القيامة { وانشق القمر } انفلق بنصفين على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Prophet’s time, Meccans requested a sign; he showed the moon split in two with Mount Hira visible between its halves.
rows.anchor: فأراهم القمر فلقتين حتى رأوا حراء بينهما، فأخبر الله تعالى أن ذلك من علامات قرب الساعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccans call the sign passing, futile magic that will go away.
rows.anchor: سحر مستمر } ذاهب باطل يذهب.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative gloss takes “mustamirr” to mean well-wrought and powerful.
rows.anchor: باطل يذهب. وقيل: محكم شديد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers’ denial and the believers’ affirmation will each reach their settled outcome when reward and punishment appear.
rows.anchor: قرار تصديق المؤمنين. يعني: عند ظهور الثواب والعقاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccans have heard reports of the destruction of earlier denying nations, which provide a final admonition.
rows.anchor: أخبار إهلاك الأمم المكذبة { ما فيه مزدجر } متناهى ومنتهى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s accounts of earlier peoples are complete wisdom without deficiency; warnings do not benefit those persisting in denial.
rows.anchor: حكمة بالغة تامة، ليس فيها نقصان، أي: القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Nudhur” is the plural of “nadhīr.”
rows.anchor: فما تغني النذر } جمع نذير، أي: فليست تغني عن التكذيب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn and humans are challenged to escape through the regions of heaven and earth, fleeing death.
rows.anchor: { يا معشر الجن والإنس إن استطعتم أن تنفذوا } تخرجوا { من أقطار السموات والأرض } نواحيها هاربين من الموت { فانفذوا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot escape; wherever they go, they encounter God’s proof and authority showing His oneness.
rows.anchor: لا تنفذون إلا بسلطان } أي: حيث ما كنتم شاهدتم حجة الله وسلطانا يدل على أنه واحد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Shuwāẓ” is flame without smoke, while “nuḥās” is smoke without flame; they are sent alternately.
rows.anchor: وهو اللهب الذي لا دخان له { ونحاس } وهو الدخان [الذي لا لهب له]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day, tongues of fire surround people, and neither jinn nor humans can defend themselves.
rows.anchor: وهو في يوم القيامة يحاط على الخلق بلسان من نار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky opens into gates for the angels to descend.
rows.anchor: انفرجت أبوابا لنزول الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky becomes rose-colored, with shifting colors like oil.
rows.anchor: في اختلاف ألوانها كالدهن واختلاف ألوانه

words: لَّا يُسْـَٔلُ عَن ذَنۢبِهِۦٓ إِنسٌۭ وَلَا جَآنٌّۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is not a question seeking information; the guilty are questioned to reproach and rebuke them.
rows.anchor: { فيومئذ لا يسأل عن ذنبه } سؤال استفهام، ولكن يسألون سؤال تقريع وتوبيخ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals are recognized by their marks: black faces and blue eyes.
rows.anchor: { يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم } بعلامتهم، وهي سواد الوجوه، وزرقة العيون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their forelocks are joined to their feet, and they are thrown into the Fire; “nawāṣī” is the plural of “nāṣiya,” forehead hair.
rows.anchor: { فيؤخذ بالنواصي والأقدام } تضم نواصيهم إلى أقدامهم، ويلقون في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Event is the coming of the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: { إذا وقعت الواقعة } جاءت القيامة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no falsehood or denial concerning its coming.
rows.anchor: { ليس لوقعتها } لمجيئها { كاذبة }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Resurrection lowers some people to the Fire and raises others to Paradise.
rows.anchor: { خافضة رافعة } تخفض قوما إلى النار، وترفع آخرين إلى الجنة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is shaken violently.
rows.anchor: حركت الأرض حركة شديدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are ground to pieces.
rows.anchor: { وبست الجبال بسا } فتت فتا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains become scattered dust.
rows.anchor: غبارا متقرقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People will be divided into three classes.
rows.anchor: { وكنتم } في ذلك اليوم { أزواجا } أصنافا { ثلاثة } ثم بين الأصناف، فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the right are those given their books in their right hands.
rows.anchor: وهم الذين يؤتون كتبهم بأيمانهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies them as those who were on Adam’s right when he brought forth the descendants from his back.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الذين كانوا على يمين آدم عليه السلام حين أخرج الذرية من ظهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question magnifies their status.
rows.anchor: { من أصحاب الميمنة } أي شيء هم؟ على التعظيم لشأنهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the left are those on the left, understood as the opposite of the preceding description.
rows.anchor: { وأصحاب المشأمة ما أصحاب المشأمة } أي: الشمال. تفسيرها على ضد تفسير التي قبلها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forerunners are those first to believe in every community and first to attain God’s mercy and Garden.
rows.anchor: { والسابقون } إلى الإيمان، من كل أمة { السابقون } إلى رحمة الله وجنته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forerunners are brought near to God’s honor.
rows.anchor: { أولئك المقربون } إلى كرامة الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is beautiful and noble, and mighty or precious.
rows.anchor: { إنه لقرآن كريم } حسن عزيز.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is kept protected with God in a guarded book.
rows.anchor: { في كتاب مكنون } مصون عند الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier disbelieving nations tasted punishment in this world for their unbelief and face painful punishment in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: ذاقوا في الدنيا العقوبة بكفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment came because messengers brought clear proofs and they rejected them.
rows.anchor: ذلك } أي: ذلك الذي نزل بهم { بأنه كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات فقالوا: أبشر يهدوننا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They considered it implausible that human beings could guide them; “human” is collective, explaining the plural “guide us.”
rows.anchor: استبعدوا أن يكون الداعي إلى الحق بشرا، والمراد بالبشر ههنا الجمع، لذلك قال: { يهدوننا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They disbelieved and turned away from faith.
rows.anchor: فكفروا وتولوا } عن الإيمان { واستغنى الله } أي: عن إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has no need of their faith or of His creatures and is praiseworthy in His actions.
rows.anchor: أي: عن إيمانهم { والله غني } عن خلقه { حميد } في أفعاله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement warns the Prophet’s wives that God could replace them with better wives if he divorced them.
rows.anchor: { عسى ربه إن طلقكن أن يبدله أزواجا خيرا منكن } هذا إخبار عن قدرة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Qānitāt” means obedient.
rows.anchor: قانتات } مطيعات { سائحات } صائمات.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Sā’iḥāt” means fasting.
rows.anchor: قانتات } مطيعات { سائحات } صائمات.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers must take themselves and their families toward what brings them near to God and keep themselves and their families from sins.
rows.anchor: يا أيها الذين آمنوا قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم نارا } أي: خذوا أنفسكم وأهليكم بما يقرب من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People and stones are the two kinds of fuel by which the Fire is kindled.
rows.anchor: وقودها الناس والحجارة } أي: توقد بهذين الجنسين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stern, strong angels who never disobey God are the keepers of Hell.
rows.anchor: عليها ملائكة غلاظ شداد لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون } يعني: خزنة جهنم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letter nūn refers to the whale on whose back the earth rests.
rows.anchor: أقسم بالحوت الذي على ظهره الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Pen is the one God created to write what will occur through the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: القلم الذي خلقه الله تعالى، فجرى بالكائنات إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who write are the angels.
rows.anchor: وما تكتب الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s favor here is His granting Muhammad prophethood, which rules out the accusation that he is mad.
rows.anchor: أي: إنك لا تكون مجنونا وقد أنعم الله عليك بالنبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers the opponents’ claim that the recipient of the Reminder is mad.
rows.anchor: وهذا جواب لقولهم: وقالوا يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر إنك لمجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s reward will neither be cut off nor diminished.
rows.anchor: غير مقطوع ولا منقوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad follows the character God commanded in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: أنت على الخلق الذي أمرك الله به في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad and the polytheists who accused him of madness will see which of them is afflicted with madness.
rows.anchor: فستبصر } يا محمد { ويبصرون } أي: المشركون الذي رموه بالجنون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether madness belongs to Muhammad or to his opponents.
rows.anchor: بأييكم المفتون } الفتنة، أبك أم بهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad must not follow the deniers in what they call him to concerning their religion.
rows.anchor: { فلا تطع المكذبين } فيما دعوك إليه من دينهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They want Muhammad to soften his stance so that they in turn will soften theirs.
rows.anchor: تلين فيلينون لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person described swears many false oaths and is contemptible.
rows.anchor: { ولا تطع كل حلاف } كثير الحلف بالباطل، أي: الوليد بن المغيرة { مهين } حقير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is a fault-finder and a tale-bearer who goes between people spreading gossip.
rows.anchor: { هماز } عياب { مشاء بنميم } ساع بين الناس بالنميمة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He withholds wealth from required dues, transgresses through oppression, and is sinful.
rows.anchor: { مناع للخير } بخيل بالمال عن الحقوق { معتد } مجاوز في الظلم { أثيم } آثم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is harsh and coarse; “after that” means in addition to the listed traits, and “zanīm” is one attached to a clan without belonging to it.
rows.anchor: { عتل } جاف غليظ { بعد ذلك } مع ما ذكرنا من أوصافه { زنيم } ملحق بقومه وليس منهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person described by this series of traits is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
rows.anchor: أي: الوليد بن المغيرة { مهين } حقير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite his wealth and sons, the man disbelieves in the Qur’an, repaying God’s favor with denial.
rows.anchor: { إن كان } لأن كان { ذا مال وبنين } يكذب بالقرآن. وهو قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Qur’an’s verses are recited to him, he calls them tales of the ancients.
rows.anchor: { إذا تتلى عليه آياتنا قال أساطير الأولين } والمعنى: أيجعل مجازاة نعمة الله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question challenges whether God would treat Muslims as criminals.
rows.anchor: { أفنجعل المسلمين كالمجرمين }. { ما لكم كيف تحكمون }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers are challenged to produce a revealed book that they study and that supports their claim to choose their afterlife outcome.
rows.anchor: { أم لكم كتاب } نزل من عند الله { فيه } ما تقولون { تدرسون } تقرون ما فيه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They claim that the book gives them whatever they choose.
rows.anchor: { إن لكم فيه } في ذلك الكتاب { لما تخيرون } تختارون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “oaths” are covenants and pledges with God, firmly binding through the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: { أم لكم أيمان } عهود ومواثيق { علينا بالغة } محكمة لا ينقطع عهدها { إلى يوم القيامة إن لكم لما تحكمون } تقضون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Inna” is read with kasra in both verses because of the lām in its response; without the lām it would properly have fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وكسرت " إن " في الآيتين لمكان اللام في جوابها، وحقها الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to ask which of them guarantees their claim to a share in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: { سلهم } يا محمد { أيهم بذلك } الذي يقولون من أن لهم في الآخرة حظا { زعيم } كفيل لهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have no partners or gods guaranteeing their claim; they should bring them if they are truthful.
rows.anchor: { أم لهم شركاء } آلهة تكفل لهم بما يقولون { فليأتوا بشركائهم } لتكفل لهم { إن كانوا صادقين } فيما يقولون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “uncovering of a shin” means the onset of a severe affair, namely the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: { يوم يكشف عن ساق } عن شدة من الأمر، وهو يوم القيامة.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this is the most severe hour of the Resurrection; “uncovering the shin” thus expresses the severity of the affair.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه: أشد ساعة في القيامة، فصار كشف الساق عبارة عن شدة الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers and hypocrites cannot prostrate: their backs become a single plate, and when they try they fall backward.
rows.anchor: { ويدعون إلى السجود } أي: الكافرون والمنافقون { فلا يستطيعون } يصير ظهرهم طبقا واحدا كلما أراد أن يسجد واحد منهم خر على قفاه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eyes are humbled and do not lift; humiliation overwhelms them.
rows.anchor: { خاشعة أبصارهم } ذليلة لا يرفعونها { ترهقهم } تغشاهم { ذلة وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In worldly life they were called to prostrate while healthy but refused to worship God.
rows.anchor: وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود } في الدنيا { وهم سالمون } فيأبون ولا يسجدون لله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Muhammad to leave the Qur’an’s deniers to Him and not be troubled, since He will handle them.
rows.anchor: { فذرني ومن يكذب بهذا الحديث } دعني والمكذبين بهذا القرآن، أي: كلهم إلي ولا تشغل قلبك بهم، فإني أكفيك أمرهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will seize them gradually, little by little, without confronting them all at once.
rows.anchor: نأخذهم قليلا قليلا ولا نباغتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God directed the storm against them as He willed.
rows.anchor: استعملها عليهم كما شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Ḥusūman” means continuous and successive; the storm cut them off and destroyed them.
rows.anchor: { حسوما } أي: دائمة متتابعة، والمعنى: تحسمهم حسوما، أي: تذهبهم وتفنيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Ṣarʿā” is the plural of “ṣarīʿ,” and refers to the people of the villages lying dead.
rows.anchor: فترى القوم } [أي: أهل القرى] { فيها } أي: في تلك الأيام { صرعى } جمع صريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They lie like fallen, hollow date-palm trunks.
rows.anchor: { كأنهم أعجاز } أصول { نخل خاوية } ساقطة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one of them remains alive.
rows.anchor: هل ترى منهم باقيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those with Pharaoh” means his followers.
rows.anchor: { وجاء فرعون ومن قبله } أي: تباعه.

rows.speaker: من قرأ
rows.claim: A reading with “min qablihi” means the nations who preceded Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ: { ومن قبله } فمعناه: من تقدمه من الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “overturned towns” are the people of Lot’s settlements.
rows.anchor: { والمؤتفكات } أي: أهل قرى قوم لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Al-khāṭiʾa” means a grave error, namely disbelief.
rows.anchor: { بالخاطئة } بالخطأ العظيم، وهو الكفر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They disobeyed their Lord’s messenger and received an increased punishment exceeding other punishments.
rows.anchor: { فعصوا رسول ربهم فأخذهم أخذة رابية } زائدة تزيد على الأخذات.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The floodwater exceeded its limit during the days of the Flood.
rows.anchor: { إنا لما طغى الماء } جاوز حده. يعني: أيام الطوفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God carried the audience’s ancestors aboard Noah’s ship.
rows.anchor: { حملناكم } أي: حملنا آباءكم { في الجارية } وهي السفينة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The drowning of Noah’s people and rescue of those with him is made a reminder so later people may heed it.
rows.anchor: تلك الفعلة التي فعلنا من إغراق قوم نوح وإنجاء من معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A receptive ear preserves what it hears.
rows.anchor: لتحفظها كل أذن تحفظ ما سمعت

words: فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌۭ وَٰحِدَةٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the first trumpet blast, which brings the Hour.
rows.anchor: { فإذا نفخ في الصور نفخة واحدة } أي: النفخة الأولى لقيام الساعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth and mountains are shattered in one blow and become scattered dust.
rows.anchor: { وحملت الأرض والجبال فدكتا } كسرتا { دكة واحدة } فصارت هباء منبثا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His proof has vanished, and his dominion and power are gone.
rows.anchor: { هلك عني سلطانيه } ذهب عني حجتي، وزال عني ملكي وقوتي، فيقول الله لخزنة جهنم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands the keepers of Hell to seize him and shackle him.
rows.anchor: { خذوه فغلوه }. { ثم الجحيم صلوه } أدخلوه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Ṣallūhu” means put him into the Fire.
rows.anchor: { ثم الجحيم صلوه } أدخلوه. { ثم في سلسلة ذرعها سبعون ذراعا فاسلكوه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is put into a seventy-cubit chain that passes through his body from anus to mouth; one link outweighs all the world’s iron combined.
rows.anchor: { ثم في سلسلة ذرعها سبعون ذراعا فاسلكوه } أي: أدخلوه في تلك السلسلة، فتدخل في دبره وتخرج من فيه، وهي سلسلة لو جمع حديد الدنيا ما وزن حلقة منها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky becomes like the dregs of oil.
rows.anchor: { يوم تكون السماء كالمهل } كدردي الزيت.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view compares it to melted tar.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كالقار المذاب، وقد مر هذا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains become like dyed wool; they are also described as jewels, or as gold, silver, and copper.
rows.anchor: { وتكون الجبال }: [الجواهر. وقيل: الذهب والفضة والنحاس] { كالعهن } كالصوف المصبوغ.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative report identifies the mountains as gold, silver, and copper; the other gloss is jewels.
rows.anchor: [الجواهر. وقيل: الذهب والفضة والنحاس] { كالعهن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No close relative asks about another because each is preoccupied with his own ordeal.
rows.anchor: لا يسأل قريب عن قريب لاشتغاله بما هو فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Relatives see and recognize one another but do not ask about one another’s condition.
rows.anchor: { يبصرونهم } يعرف بعضهم بعضا، أي: إن الحميم يرى حميمه ويعرفه، ولا يسأل عن شأنه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbeliever wishes to ransom himself from that day’s punishment with his children, wife, and brother.
rows.anchor: { وصاحبته } وزوجته { وأخيه }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His “faṣīla” is the clan from which he separated, which shelters him through kinship.
rows.anchor: { وفصيلته } عشيرته التي فصل منها { التي تؤويه } تضمه إليها في النسب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was informed by revelation from God.
rows.anchor: { قل أوحي إلي } أي: أخبرت بالوحي من الله إلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent a group of jinn to listen to the Prophet reciting the dawn prayer at Batn Nakhlah; they are the group mentioned in Sūrat al-Aḥqāf.
rows.anchor: بعث نفرا من الجن ليستمعوا قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي الصبح ببطن نخلة، وهؤلاء الذين ذكرهم الله في سورة الأحقاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On returning to their people, the jinn called the Qur’an amazing for its eloquence, clarity, and truthful reports.
rows.anchor: { إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا } في فصاحته وبيانه وصدق إخباره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad need not worry about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra; God will handle him. He was created alone, without wealth or children.
rows.anchor: { ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا } أي: لا تهتم لشأنه فإني أكفيك أمره، أي: الوليد بن المغيرة، يقول: خلقته وحيدا لا ولد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His wealth was continuous and abundant from crops, livestock, and trade.
rows.anchor: دائما لا ينقطع عنه من الزرع والضرع والتجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He had ten sons present with him in Mecca.
rows.anchor: { وبنين شهودا } حضورا معه بمكة، وكانوا عشرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God spread out comfort, livelihood, and wealth for him.
rows.anchor: بسطت له في العيش والمال بسطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite these gifts, he hopes for yet more wealth and children.
rows.anchor: يرجو أن أزيده مالا وولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Kallā” cuts off his hope.
rows.anchor: { كلا } قطع لرجائه { إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا } للقرآن معاندا غير مطيع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He stubbornly opposed the Qur’an’s signs and refused obedience.
rows.anchor: للقرآن معاندا غير مطيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will overwhelm him with hardship in punishment.
rows.anchor: سأغشيه مشقة من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Quraysh asked what he would say about Muhammad, al-Walīd considered what he could say about Muhammad and the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: سألته ما تقول في محمد؟ فتفكر في نفسه وقدر القول في محمد عليه السلام والقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Faqutila” means cursed and punished; “how did he determine?” is an expression of astonishment.
rows.anchor: { فقتل } لعن وعذب { كيف قدر }؟ استفهام على طريق التعجب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He then looked.
rows.anchor: { ثم نظر }. { ثم عبس وبسر } كلح وجهه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He frowned and grimaced.
rows.anchor: { ثم عبس وبسر } كلح وجهه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He turned away and grew arrogant toward faith.
rows.anchor: { ثم أدبر واستكبر } عن الإيمان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He claimed that Muhammad’s recitation was magic transmitted from sorcerers.
rows.anchor: { فقال إن هذا } ما هذا الذي يقرؤه محمد { إلا سحر يؤثر } يروى عن السحرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that this is human speech echoes the assertion that a human teaches Muhammad.
rows.anchor: { إن هذا إلا قول البشر } كما قالوا:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will admit him to Hell.
rows.anchor: { سأصليه سقر } سأدخله جهنم، ثم أعلم عظم شأن سقر من العذاب، فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question tells the hearer of the immense severity of Saqar’s punishment.
rows.anchor: ما أعلمك أي شيء سقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saqar burns the skin until it turns black.
rows.anchor: محرقة للجلد حتى تسوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There are nineteen keepers; one can push into Hell more people than the tribes of Rabīʿa and Muḍar.
rows.anchor: { عليها تسعة عشر } من الخزنة، الواحدة منهم يدفع بالدفعة الواحدة في جهنم أكثر من ربيعة ومضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the verse came down, a polytheist boasted he could handle seventeen of the keepers and asked others to handle two.
rows.anchor: فلما نزلت هذه الآية قال بعض المشركين: أنا أكفيكم منهم سبعة عشر، فاكفوني اثنين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers of the Fire are angels, not men, so no one can overpower them.
rows.anchor: { وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملائكة } لا رجالا، فمن ذا يغلب الملائكة؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The small number tests disbelievers, who scoff that Muhammad has only nineteen helpers.
rows.anchor: { وما جعلنا عدتهم } عددهم في القلة { إلا فتنة للذين كفروا } لأنهم قالوا: ما أعوان محمد إلا تسعة عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People given scripture gain certainty because Muhammad’s message agrees with their books.
rows.anchor: { ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب } ليعلموا أن ما أتى به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم موافق لما في كتبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers grow in faith by affirming the Messenger and the reported number of Hell’s keepers.
rows.anchor: { ويزداد الذين آمنوا } لأنهم يصدقون بما أتى به الرسول عليه السلام، وبعدد خزنة النار

words: وَلَا يَرْتَابَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of scripture and believers do not doubt the number Muhammad reported.
rows.anchor: { ولا يرتاب الذين أوتوا الكتاب والمؤمنون } أي: لا يشكون في أن عددهم على ما أخبر به محمد عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sickness in their hearts is doubt; they and the disbelievers ask what God intends by this number as an example.
rows.anchor: { وليقول الذين في قلوبهم مرض } شك { والكافرون ماذا أراد الله بهذا مثلا } أي: شيء أراد الله بهذا العدد وتخصيصه؟

words: كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God misguides and guides whom He wills, as He has led the deniers astray for their rejection.
rows.anchor: { كذلك } كما أضلهم الله بتكذيبهم { يضل الله من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء

words: وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This answers those who asked why Muhammad’s helpers number only nineteen: only God knows His forces.
rows.anchor: ما أعوانه إلا تسعة عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire reminds people in this life of the Fire awaiting them in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: { وما هي } أي: النار { إلا ذكرى للبشر } أي: إنها تذكرهم في الدنيا النار في الآخرة.

words: لَا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِۦ لِسَانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِۦٓ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Gabriel recited the Qur’an, the Prophet repeated it before he finished for fear of forgetting; God assured him He would preserve and gather it in his heart.
rows.anchor: كان جبريل عليه السلام إذا نزل بالقرآن تلاه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل فراغ جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God undertakes to gather and recite the Qur’an to the Prophet so he understands it.
rows.anchor: قراءته عليك حتى تعيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should follow the recitation and not hurry ahead before Gabriel has finished.
rows.anchor: { فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه } أي: لا تعجل بالتلاوة إلى أن يقرأ عليك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God undertakes to reveal it as a Qur’an containing clarification for people.
rows.anchor: علينا أن ننزله قرآنا فيه بيان للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke warns that people prefer worldly life to the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: { كلا } زجر وتنبيه. { بل تحبون العاجلة }. { وتذرون الآخرة } أي: تختارون الدنيا على العقبى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bright faces of the blessed will see their Creator directly.
rows.anchor: { وجوه يومئذ } يوم القيامة { ناضرة } مضيئة حسنة. { إلى ربها ناظرة } تنظر إلى خالقها عيانا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other faces will be gloomy and grim.
rows.anchor: { ووجوه يومئذ باسرة } كالحة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They know a devastating calamity of punishment will be inflicted on them.
rows.anchor: { تظن } توقن { أن يفعل بها فاقرة } داهية عظيمة من العذاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What reaches the collarbones is the soul.
rows.anchor: { كلا إذا بلغت التراقي } يعني: النفس. بلغت عظام الحلق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those present at the dying person’s side ask for a doctor or an exorcist who might cure him by recitation.
rows.anchor: { وقيل من راق } مال من حضر ذلك الذي قارب الموت: هل من طبيب يداويه، وراق يرقيه فيشفى برقيته؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dying person realizes death separates him from worldly life, family, and wealth.
rows.anchor: { وظن } أيقن الذي نزل به الموت { أنه الفراق } من الدنيا والأهل والمال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destination and return are to God, as angels drive the spirit where He commands.
rows.anchor: المنتهى والمرجع بسوق الملائكة الروح إلى حيث أمر الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who neither affirmed nor prayed is Abū Jahl.
rows.anchor: { فلا صدق ولا صلى } يعني: أبا جهل لعنه الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He denied the message and turned away from faith.
rows.anchor: { ولكن كذب وتولى } عن الإيمان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He went back to his family strutting proudly.
rows.anchor: { ثم ذهب إلى أهله يتمطى } يتبختر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated phrase threatens Abū Jahl with harm: misfortune has clung to him.
rows.anchor: { أولى لك فأولى }. { ثم أولى لك فأولى } هذا تهديد ووعيد له، والمعنى: وليك المكروه يا أبا أجهل، [أي: لزمك المكروه].

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person is not left neglected, without commands or prohibitions.
rows.anchor: مهملا غير مأمور ولا منهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person began as semen poured into the womb.
rows.anchor: { ألم يك نطفة من مني يمنى } يصب في الرحم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God formed him from a clot into a complete human being.
rows.anchor: { ثم كان علقة فخلق فسوى } فخلقه الله فسوى خلقه، حتى صار إنسانا بعد أن كان علقة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made from the human two kinds: male and female.
rows.anchor: فخلق من الإنسان صنفين الرجل والمرأة

words: أَلَيْسَ ذَٰلِكَ بِقَٰدِرٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يُحْـِۧىَ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The One who did this is surely able to resurrect the dead and has power over all things.
rows.anchor: الذي فعل هذا { بقادر على أن يحيي الموتى }؟ [بلى، وهو على كل شيء قدير].

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sinner is ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa, and the unbeliever is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
rows.anchor: { ولا تطع منهم آثما } يعني: عتبة بن ربيعة { أو كفورا } يعني: الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two men promised the Prophet wealth and marriage if he stopped calling them to Islam.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهما ضمنا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المال والتزويج إن ترك دعوتهم إلى الإسلام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are uprooted from their places and swept away quickly.
rows.anchor: { وإذا الجبال نسفت } قلعت من أماكنها، فأذهبت بسرعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers are gathered at their appointed time, the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: { وإذا الرسل أقتت } جمعت لوقت، وهو يوم القيامة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question magnifies the day to which judgment is delayed.
rows.anchor: { لأي يوم أجلت } أخرت وأمهلت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Decision is the judgment between people.
rows.anchor: { ليوم الفصل } القضاء بين الناس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question magnifies that day, followed by woe for deniers.
rows.anchor: { وما أدراك ما يوم الفصل } على التعظيم لذلك اليوم. { ويل يومئذ للمكذبين }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroyed the earlier communities that denied the truth.
rows.anchor: من الأمم المكذبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Later people who follow the same path of disbelief and denial are made to follow them.
rows.anchor: ممن سلكوا سبيلهم في الكفر والتكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does likewise to criminals, meaning the deniers among Muhammad’s people.
rows.anchor: { كذلك } مثل الذي فعلنا بهم { نفعل بالمجرمين } بالمكذبين من قومك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contemptible fluid is sperm.
rows.anchor: { ألم نخلقكم من ماء مهين } أي: النطفة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure resting place is the womb.
rows.anchor: { فجعلناه في قرار مكين } أي: الرحم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed measure is the time of birth.
rows.anchor: وهو وقت الولادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading “qaddarnā” with doubling and “qadarnā” without it are two forms with the same meaning: appointing the time of birth.
rows.anchor: { فقدرنا } أي: قدرنا وقت الولادة { فنعم القادرون } فنعم المقدرون نحن، وقرئت بالتشديد والتخفيف، لغتان بمعنى واحد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell watches for the disbelievers, who cannot pass beyond it.
rows.anchor: { إن جهنم كانت مرصادا } ترصد أهل الكفر، فلا يجاوزونها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The transgressors” means the disbelievers; Hell is their return.
rows.anchor: { للطاغين } للكافرين { مآبا } مرجعا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Aḥqāb” is plural of “ḥuqb”: eighty years of 360 days, each day like a thousand worldly years; when one term ends another follows without end.
rows.anchor: { لابثين } ماكثين { فيها أحقابا } جمع حقب، وهو ثمانون سنة، كل سنة ثلثمائة وستون يوما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blast of resurrection follows the earthquake.
rows.anchor: { تتبعها الرادفة } يعني: نفخة البعث تأتي بعد الزلزلة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hearts are agitated and displaced, and their eyes humbled.
rows.anchor: { قلوب يومئذ واجفة } قلقة زائلة عن أماكنها. { أبصارها خاشعة } ذليلة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers of resurrection ask whether they will be returned to their former life after death, even once their bones have decayed.
rows.anchor: { يقولون } يعني: منكري البعث { أإنا لمردودون في الحافرة } أي: إلى أول الأمر من الحياة بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call such a return a losing one.
rows.anchor: رجعة يخسر فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God shows resurrection is easy: it takes only one cry and blast, after which they are on the earth’s surface instead of underground.
rows.anchor: { فإنما هي زجرة واحدة } أي: صيحة ونفخة. { فإذا هم بالساهرة } يعني: وجه الأرض بعد ما كانوا في بطنها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Moses is addressed to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: { هل أتاك } يا محمد { حديث موسى }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭuwā is the name of the sacred valley.
rows.anchor: طوى اسم ذلك الوادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh had exceeded the bounds through disbelief.
rows.anchor: { اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى } جاوز الحد في الكفر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is to ask Pharaoh whether he wants to purify himself from disbelief by believing.
rows.anchor: أترغب في أن تتطهر من كفرك بالإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet frowned and turned away.
rows.anchor: { عبس } كلح { وتولى } أعرض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm came while the Prophet was inviting Quraysh leaders to Islam, repeatedly calling without realizing the Prophet was occupied; the Prophet’s displeasure showed, he turned away, and these verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: { جاءه الأعمى } وهو عبد الله بن أم مكتوم أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يدعوا أشراف قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind man might purify himself from sin through Islam or take heed so the reminder benefits him; he had come seeking Islam and asking to be taught what God taught the Prophet.
rows.anchor: لعل الأعمى { يزكى } يتطهر من ذنوبه بالإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “One who deems himself self-sufficient” means someone made wealthy.
rows.anchor: { أما من استغنى } أثرى من المال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet turns toward and attends to the wealthy man.
rows.anchor: { فأنت له تصدى } تقبل عليه وتتعرض له.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not responsible if the man does not accept Islam; his duty is only to convey the message.
rows.anchor: { وما عليك ألا يزكى } أي شيء عليك في أن لا يسلم؛ لأنه ليس عليك إسلامه، إنما عليك البلاغ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who came eagerly and feared God is the blind man.
rows.anchor: { وأما من جاءك يسعى } أي: الأعمى. { وهو يخشى } الله تعالى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was distracted from the blind man.
rows.anchor: { فأنت عنه تلهى } تتشاغل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Kallā” rebukes and stops this conduct.
rows.anchor: { كلا } ردع وزجر، أي: لا تفعل مثل ما فعلت { إنها } إن آيات القرآن { تذكرة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s verses are a reminder for creation, and whoever wishes may remember the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: { فمن شاء ذكره } يعني: القرآن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s exalted status is shown by its being in honored sheets in God’s Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبر بجلالته في اللوح المحفوظ عنده، [فقال]: { في صحف مكرمة }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sheets are elevated in rank and purified; only the purified touch them.
rows.anchor: { مرفوعة } رفيعة القدر { مطهرة } لا يمسها إلا المطهرون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scribes are angels.
rows.anchor: { بأيدي سفرة } كتبة، وهم الملائكة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Barara” is the plural of “bārr,” righteous.
rows.anchor: { كرام بررة } جمع بار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Qutila” is a curse against the unbeliever, identified as ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab.
rows.anchor: { قتل الإنسان } لعن الكافر. يعني: عتبة بن أبي لهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means: how intense is his unbelief.
rows.anchor: ما أشد كفره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is rhetorical confirmation, after which God explains the stages of creation.
rows.anchor: { من أي شيء خلقه } استفهام معناه التقرير، ثم فسر فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God proportioned the human through stages from a clot and morsel until birth from the mother’s womb.
rows.anchor: أطوارا من علقة ومضغة إلى أن خرج من بطن أمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky splits open.
rows.anchor: { إذا السماء انفطرت } انشقت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stars fall apart and scatter.
rows.anchor: { وإذا الكواكب انتثرت } تساقطت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seas are opened into one another and become a single sea.
rows.anchor: فتح بعضها في بعض فصارت بحرا واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The graves are overturned, their soil turned over, and their dead raised.
rows.anchor: قلب ترابها وبعث الموتى الذين فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each soul learns what commanded acts it performed and what it left undone.
rows.anchor: { علمت نفس ما قدمت } من عمل أمرت به { و } ما { أخرت } منه فلم تعمله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks what deceived a person into adorning falsehood and neglecting what God required.
rows.anchor: { يا أيها الإنسان ما غرك بربك الكريم } أي: ما خدعك وسول لك الباطل حتى أضعت ما أوجب عليك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the human’s creation proportionate and upright in form and stature.
rows.anchor: { الذي خلقك فسواك } جعلك مستوي الخلق { فعدلك } قومك وجعلك معتدل الخلق والقامة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Paradise look at the blessings and honor God has given them.
rows.anchor: { على الأرائك ينظرون } أي: إلى ما أعطاهم الله سبحانه من النعيم والكرامة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The freshness of bliss shows as glow and brightness on their faces.
rows.anchor: { تعرف في وجوههم نضرة النعيم } أي: غضارته وبريقه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Raḥīq” is pure wine, and it is sealed.
rows.anchor: { يسقون من رحيق } وهو الخمر الصافية. { مختوم }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the cup is emptied and the drink ends, it is capped with the scent of musk.
rows.anchor: { ختامه مسك } يعني: إذا فني ما في الكأس وانقطع الشراب يختم ذلك الشراب برائحة المسك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who aspire should compete by hastening to obey God.
rows.anchor: فليرغب الراغبون بالمبادرة إلى طاعة الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasnim is a spring flowing in the Garden of Eden, the highest of the gardens.
rows.anchor: { ومزاجه } ومزاج ذلك الشراب { من تسنيم } وهو عين ماء تجري في جنة عدن، وهي أعلى الجنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those brought near drink from that spring directly.
rows.anchor: { عينا يشرب بها المقربون } أي: يشربها المقربون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those who committed crimes” means the polytheists, specifically Abū Jahl and his companions, who mocked poor believers.
rows.anchor: { إن الذين أجرموا } أشركوا: يعني: أبا جهل وأصحابه { كانوا من الذين آمنوا } من فقراء المؤمنين { يضحكون } استهزاء بهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night visitor is all the stars, which appear at night; anything arriving at night is called a visitor, and the piercing star is bright and radiant.
rows.anchor: { والسماء والطارق } يعني: النجوم كلها؛ لأن طلوعها بالليل، وكل ما أتى ليلا فهو طارق، وقد فسر الله تعالى ذلك بقوله: { النجم الثاقب } المضيء النير.

words: إِن كُلُّ نَفْسٍۢ لَّمَّا عَلَيْهَا حَافِظٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Mā” is an extra particle; the meaning is that every soul has a guardian from its Lord protecting its deeds.
rows.anchor: { إن كل نفس لما عليها } لعليها، و { ما } صلة { حافظ } من ربها يحفظ عملها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human is asked to consider what substance his Lord created him from.
rows.anchor: { فلينظر الإنسان مم خلق } من أي شيء خلقه ربه، ثم بين فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ejected fluid is semen poured into the womb: the man’s fluid comes from the backbone and the woman’s from the chest bones.
rows.anchor: { خلق من ماء دافق } مدفوق مصبوب في الرحم. يعني: النطفة. { يخرج من بين الصلب } وهو ماء الرجل { والترائب } عظام الصدر، وهو ماء المرأة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is able to resurrect and restore the human after death.
rows.anchor: { إنه } إن الله { على رجعه } على بعث الإنسان وإعادته بعد الموت { لقادر }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day, hidden duties between a servant and God, such as prayer, fasting, and ritual bathing, are tested and exposed; their truthfulness becomes clear.
rows.anchor: { يوم تبلى السرائر } يعني: يوم القيامة، وفي ذلك اليوم تختبر السرائر

words: فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن قُوَّةٍۢ وَلَا نَاصِرٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelieving human has no strength and no helper.
rows.anchor: { فما له } يعني: الإنسان الكافر { من قوة ولا ناصر }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky’s “return” is rain.
rows.anchor: { والسماء ذات الرجع } أي: المطر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth’s splitting is its opening for plants to grow.
rows.anchor: { والأرض ذات الصدع } تتشقق عن النبات.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an decisively distinguishes truth from falsehood and is neither play nor falsehood.
rows.anchor: { إنه } أي: القرآن { لقول فصل } يفصل بين الحق والباطل. { وما هو بالهزل } أي: باللعب والباطل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan polytheists outwardly present one attitude to the Prophet while secretly acting against him.
rows.anchor: { إنهم } يعني: مشركي مكة { يكيدون كيدا } يظهرون للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على ما هم على خلافه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s counterplot is to draw them on gradually without their awareness.
rows.anchor: { وأكيد كيدا } وهو استدارج الله تعالى إياهم من حيث لا يعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Muhammad to delay them briefly before punishment; they were seized at Badr after the Prophet prayed against them and received this command.
rows.anchor: أخرهم قليلا؛ فإني آخذهم بالعذاب، فأخذوا يوم بدر
